fields.description: Analytical Quality Assurance applied (internal + external QA per §2.1).
fields.verification_quote: Analytical Quality Assurance (AQA): Measures for supporting own research results under controlled conditions. Analytical quality assurance comprises internal and external quality control. — printed p.8

Besides the advice on the practical application of operating methods, this Standard defines quality requirements that - if implemented - allow equal treatment. By taking into account these measures, the operating methods correspond to the requirements of § 4 AbwV (German Waste Water Ordinance); there are no reasons that oppose their application as equal methods in the determinations in the discharge consent from a metrological point of view. — printed p.7

Analytical Quality Assurance (AQA): Measures for supporting own research results under controlled conditions. Analytical quality assurance comprises internal and external quality control. — printed p.8

For measuring, the material, reagents and measuring system are to a large extent prepared by the manufacturer. Thus, in their handling fewer steps are needed in comparison to reference methods. However, under disadvantageous matrices, problems might occur in the application. To notice such disturbing influences, the corresponding measures must be taken regularly, which are described in this Standard and which assure quality (plausibility checks, parallel analyses). — printed p.10

fields.label_de: Nachweis: 3.2 Requirements on the Manufacturers of Analytical Devices and Reagents
fields.verification_quote: Information on the expiry date and the storage conditions of the reagents must be attached to the packing in a clearly visible way. — printed p.10

fields.label_de: Nachweis: 3.2 Requirements on the Manufacturers of Analytical Devices and Reagents
fields.verification_quote: Advice on an appropriate function control (inspection equipment monitoring) must be given. — printed p.10

fields.label_de: Nachweis: 3.2 Requirements on the Manufacturers of Analytical Devices and Reagents
fields.verification_quote: Changes in the handling (e. g. factor alterations in the photometric determination) must be communicated up-to-date and clearly. — printed p.10

The user must be aware of the fact that also when applying the operating methods properly incorrect measurements higher results or lower results) can occur due to the composition of the sample. Due to quality assuring measures the user should be able to notice such incorrect measurements and to prevent them. — printed p.10

When applying operating methods, the operator must take or organise the following measures together with the operating personnel: a) basic instruction, b) successive supervision, c) regular training measures, d) provision of written operating instructions for all important working steps, e) regular quality control. — printed p.10

fields.description: Which IGC-Card module documents the QA measure (Cards 1-11).
fields.verification_quote: The Annex of DWA-A 704E represents a working aid and consists of eleven IQC-Cards that, if put together, represent the framework of quality control for operating analysis. | Survey Card IQC-Card 1 | Internal Specifications IQC-Card 2 | Multiple Determinations IQC-Card 3 | Measurement of Standards IQC-Card 4 | Plausibility Checks IQC-Card 5 | Equivalency Measurements IQC-Card 6 | Parallel Analyses to the Reference Methods IQC-Card 7 | Sampling IQC-Card 8 | Test Equipment Monitoring IQC-Card 9 | Personnel Record Sheet Operating Analysis IQC-Card 10 | Deviations and Measures IQC-Card 11 — printed p.17

fields.description: Changes in the handling (e.g. by factor alterations in the production / determination) are communicated up-to-date and clearly (§3.2).
fields.verification_quote: Changes in the handling (e. g. factor alterations in the photometric determination) must be communicated up-to-date and clearly. — printed p.10

fields.description: Manufacturer provides comprehensible work and user instructions for the method (§3.2).
fields.verification_quote: Comprehensible and clear work instructions must be provided. — printed p.10

fields.description: Manufacturer provides an appropriate function control for the operating analysis system (§3.2).
fields.verification_quote: Advice on an appropriate function control (inspection equipment monitoring) must be given. — printed p.10

fields.description: Operating method has been evaluated for the whole working range and validated where possible (§3.1).
fields.verification_quote: The operating methods must: be feasible on-site without great time effort, show a possibly high accuracy and a good selectivity, be easy to handle, be specifically applicable for the single case of application, be checked regularly by parallel analyses with the respective reference methods, correspond to the valid work safety regulations, be environmentally friendly in their use and disposal. — printed p.10

fields.description: Operating method results compared/validated against an accepted reference method (§3.1, §4.2).
fields.verification_quote: The operating methods must: be feasible on-site without great time effort, show a possibly high accuracy and a good selectivity, be easy to handle, be specifically applicable for the single case of application, be checked regularly by parallel analyses with the respective reference methods, correspond to the valid work safety regulations, be environmentally friendly in their use and disposal. | To prove the suitability of a new operating method or the comparability of the results in connection with difficult wastewaters, parallel analysis, which is described in the following, can be used. The results of the operating method are contrasted with those of the reference method. — printed p.10 and 11

fields.description: User applies the method exactly as described in the operating instruction leaflet (§3.3).
fields.verification_quote: The application of operating methods in wastewater systems requires analytic-chemically trained personnel. The users of operating methods should therefore possess the educational or qualification level of at least a sewage engineering technician or a comparative training. — printed p.10

fields.label_en: Internal quality control performed by user
fields.description: User regularly performs the internal quality-control measures (IGC) - cf. Annex A (§3.3).
fields.verification_quote: When applying operating methods, the operator must take or organise the following measures together with the operating personnel: a) basic instruction, b) successive supervision, c) regular training measures, d) provision of written operating instructions for all important working steps, e) regular quality control. | Possibilities for quality controls in the sense of Section 4.4 must be given. — printed p.10

fields.description: Mode of application of the operating method: parallel to reference method, single substitute, or (self-monitoring) use criteria (§4.1).
fields.verification_quote: For the reasonable application of operating methods the following guidelines apply: When pertaining to water and wastewater fee regulations, operating methods can only replace reference methods if this is regulated by law. [...] The use of operating methods can clearly reduce the need for reference methods. So, for example, in self-monitoring - except for the parallel analysis - reference methods can be omitted. — printed p.11

By referring to the criteria mentioned in Sections 3.1 and 3.2, the operator must decide for the operating method that is suitable for his specific case of application. In doing so, especially the measuring range must be selected in such way that preferably the expected result can be found in the 20 % to 80 % interval of the measuring range. From experience, this range shows the greatest analytical reliability. Suitable dilution steps are permitted. — printed p.11

By referring to the criteria mentioned in Sections 3.1 and 3.2, the operator must decide for the operating method that is suitable for his specific case of application. In doing so, especially the measuring range must be selected in such way that preferably the expected result can be found in the 20 % to 80 % interval of the measuring range. From experience, this range shows the greatest analytical reliability. Suitable dilution steps are permitted. — printed p.11

An intensive basic instruction must be carried out according to the following factors: overview of the parameters to be analysed, introduction to parameter-specific sampling including the required pre-treatment of samples and preservation, practice of the operating method for each parameter with representative wastewater samples of the planned cases of application (autonomous completion and handling) according to the given work instruction, — printed p.11

The skills and knowledge imparted in the basic instruction must be deepened and updated in regular training. Special importance must be attached to the thorough gathering, documentation, and interpretation of the measuring results. | For seizing the results of operating methods, regular training courses (e. g. annually) are necessary. [...] Essential components of regular training courses must therefore include the following points: proper use of pipettes and their regular check, selection of suitable test kits and measuring ranges, regular check of the equipment used such as thermoreactors and photometers, qualified and regular use of IQC-Cards. — printed p.12

In doing so, especially the measuring range must be selected in such way that preferably the expected result can be found in the 20 % to 80 % interval of the measuring range. From experience, this range shows the greatest analytical reliability. Suitable dilution steps are permitted. — printed p.11

fields.description: Selected operating method established as suitable per Sec. 3 and §4.2 (referring to the criteria mentioned in Sections 3.1 and 3.2).
fields.verification_quote: By referring to the criteria mentioned in Sections 3.1 and 3.2, the operator must decide for the operating method that is suitable for his specific case of application. In doing so, especially the measuring range must be selected in such way that preferably the expected result can be found in the 20 % to 80 % interval of the measuring range. From experience, this range shows the greatest analytical reliability. Suitable dilution steps are permitted. — printed p.11

fields.description: Method should be selected such that at least 80 % of the measuring range is covered when validating against the reference method (§4.2).
fields.verification_quote: By referring to the criteria mentioned in Sections 3.1 and 3.2, the operator must decide for the operating method that is suitable for his specific case of application. In doing so, especially the measuring range must be selected in such way that preferably the expected result can be found in the 20 % to 80 % interval of the measuring range. From experience, this range shows the greatest analytical reliability. Suitable dilution steps are permitted. — printed p.11

fields.description: Intensive basic instruction carried out per §4.3.1 (overview of parameters, sampling/preservation, practical exercise, sources of error).
fields.verification_quote: An intensive basic instruction must be carried out according to the following factors: overview of the parameters to be analysed, introduction to parameter-specific sampling including the required pre-treatment of samples and preservation, practice of the operating method for each parameter with representative wastewater samples of the planned cases of application (autonomous completion and handling) according to the given work instruction, — printed p.11

fields.description: Updated/repeated instruction at regular intervals (successive supervision) per §4.3.2.
fields.verification_quote: The skills and knowledge imparted in the basic instruction must be deepened and updated in regular training. Special importance must be attached to the thorough gathering, documentation, and interpretation of the measuring results. — printed p.12

fields.description: Training courses on proper use of pipettes/measuring ranges, equipment checks, thermometers/IGC-Cards (§4.3.3); external courses may complement in-house training.
fields.verification_quote: For seizing the results of operating methods, regular training courses (e. g. annually) are necessary. [...] Essential components of regular training courses must therefore include the following points: proper use of pipettes and their regular check, selection of suitable test kits and measuring ranges, regular check of the equipment used such as thermoreactors and photometers, qualified and regular use of IQC-Cards. — printed p.12

fields.label_de: Nachweis: 4.4 Quality Controls, Plausibility of the Measuring Results
fields.verification_quote: When using operating methods, the operator must pay special attention to quality control (see also Annex A). This ensures that the handling, the reagents used and the measuring equipment are checked regularly as follows: check of the reproducibility of a sample by multiple determination, measuring of standard solutions to check the procedure, the measurement equipment and reagents, parallel analyses as a comparison to reference methods, [...] check of plausibility by dilution and standard addition of the wastewater sample, [...] control of the reagents' storage life. — printed p.12

fields.label_de: Nachweis: 4.4 Quality Controls, Plausibility of the Measuring Results
fields.verification_quote: In most cases, the user of operating methods will carry out the sampling/pre-treatment of samples him-/herself. This is why an introduction to the importance of sampling, the problems related to it, the selection of suitable sampling equipment and the sample containers as well as the transport of samples and pre-treatment of samples must be given. [...] The sampling and pre-treatment must be documented (e. g. in the operation log). — printed p.13

fields.description: Control (plausibility) by blank value and standard addition / control of standard and blank value of the wastewater sample (§4.4 e).
fields.verification_quote: check of plausibility by dilution and standard addition of the wastewater sample, — printed p.12

fields.description: Equivalency measurement by treatment plant operating methods, intra-laboratory test (§4.4 d).
fields.verification_quote: equivalency measurements by means of operating methods from other wastewater systems (e.g. within the scope of wastewater treatment plant neighbourhoods) and/or participation in interlaboratory tests, — printed p.12

fields.description: Measurement of standard solutions to check the procedure (multiple determination), §4.4 b).
fields.verification_quote: measuring of standard solutions to check the procedure, the measurement equipment and reagents, — printed p.12

fields.description: Parallel analyses as a comparison to reference methods (§4.4 c).
fields.verification_quote: parallel analyses as a comparison to reference methods, — printed p.12

fields.description: Control of the storage life / maintenance of the reagents' storage life (§4.4).
fields.verification_quote: control of the reagents' storage life. | Control of the storage life of the reagents: Usually, the reagents have a storage life of 2 years if stored in a dry, dark and cool place. Only few tests have a reduced storage life, 12 and/or 18 months, or must be stored refrigerated. The expiry date is given on the packing. [...] Quarterly, the stock should be checked and all expired sets should be disposed of. — printed p.12 and 55

fields.description: Check of the reproducibility of a sample by multiple determination (§4.4 a).
fields.verification_quote: This ensures that the handling, the reagents used and the measuring equipment are checked regularly as follows: check of the reproducibility of a sample by multiple determination, — printed p.12

fields.description: Which container material is suitable for storage of the sample (IGC-Card 8).
fields.verification_quote: Which container material is suitable for sampling? Changes of the sample due to interactions with the container material must be eliminated. | Were the containers thoroughly cleaned before the re-use and were flushed with fully desalinated water? Sample enrichment/carry-over by pre-flushing with contaminated water or wastewater residues must be prevented. — printed p.49

fields.description: Maximum storage time before analysis (IGC-Card 8 storage of samples).
fields.verification_quote: Storage of samples: What is the optimum storage temperature to eliminate changes of the sample in the best possible way? The wastewater sample should be stored at temperatures around 4 °C for a short time. In this way, for instance, the bacterial conversion of ammonium to nitrate can be suppressed. | Besides the current measuring results, all boundary conditions must be documented. Among those are time (or period), type and location of the sampling, type and duration of the storage, measures for pre-treatment (e. g. preservation) of the sample, information on the method of analysis, etc. — printed p.49 and 13

fields.description: On-site assessment: influence of precipitation (none / partial / full) recorded on the sampling log (IGC-Card 8).
fields.verification_quote: IQC-Card 8 - Sampling, Sampling Log: Pre-treatment: none [ ] cooled [ ] added: ______ | Influence of precipitation: yes [ ] no [ ] — printed p.51

fields.description: Pre-treatment: homogenisation, filtration, decomposition (IGC-Card 8); needed for some parameters (e.g. P_total).
fields.verification_quote: Pre-treatment of the samples: Is a homogenisation of the sample urgently necessary and/or reasonable? [...] The homogenisation is carried out according to DIN 38402-30 if not regulated otherwise. | Is a filtration of the sample before the photometrical measurement necessary or possible? [...] Is a thermal-chemical digestion necessary? [...] Is a dilution of the sample necessary? If the measurement range is exceeded, the sample must be diluted and/or another measurement range must be used. — printed p.49-50

fields.description: Type of sample taken: single sample, random sample, mixed sample, qualified sample (IGC-Card 8).
fields.verification_quote: The sampling of a wastewater sample can be carried out as single, random, qualified random or mixed sample: Single sample: A random (with reference to time and/or location) sample gained by single taking (mostly by scooping) from a body of water. | Random sample: One or several single samples taken in subsequent order to analyse the current condition. | Mixed sample: Two or several samples or semi-samples that are continuously taken and mixed in an adequate ratio in order to determine the average value of a certain parameter. | Qualified random sample: Special type of a mixed sample consisting of at least five random samples that are taken within a period of maximally two hours in intervals of not less than two minutes and are mixed. — printed p.49

fields.description: Method of sampling: manual or automatic; time-/volume-/flow-proportional (IGC-Card 8 Sampling Log).
fields.verification_quote: IQC-Card 8 - Sampling, Sampling Log, Method of sampling: manual sampling [ ] - automatic sampling [ ] time proportional [ ] volume proportional [ ] flow proportional [ ] — printed p.51

fields.description: Storage temperature to slow changes of the substances in the test (sample stored as cold as possible, e.g. refrigerator); ammonification slowed by low temperature (IGC-Card 8).
fields.verification_quote: Storage of samples: What is the optimum storage temperature to eliminate changes of the sample in the best possible way? The wastewater sample should be stored at temperatures around 4 °C for a short time. In this way, for instance, the bacterial conversion of ammonium to nitrate can be suppressed. — printed p.49

fields.label_de: Nachweis: 5.1 Documentation of the Measuring Results
fields.verification_quote: Taking into account the above listed notes on quality control is a prerequisite for correct analysis results of a constant high quality. However, the data only achieves an adequate meaning if the circumstances of their survey and the further measures taken for quality assurance are documented in a suitable form, e. g. by means of IQC-Cards. — printed p.13

All measures described under Item 4.4, which are carried out for quality control, must be documented concisely and extensively. This especially enables the operating staff and external staff to gain an objective impression of the quality of the collected data. The documentation can, for instance, be performed in the form of IQC-Cards, which record each quality control measure. — printed p.13

fields.label_de: Nachweis: 5.3 Documentation of the Staff's Qualification
fields.verification_quote: Within the scope of the documentation, a constant up-to-date overview of the staff's qualification as well as of the participation in regular training measures should be kept. This allows the proof that measurements or sampling were carried out by qualified staff. — printed p.13

fields.description: Up-to-date overview of staff qualification & training maintained (§5.3, IGC-Card 10).
fields.verification_quote: Within the scope of the documentation, a constant up-to-date overview of the staff's qualification as well as of the participation in regular training measures should be kept. This allows the proof that measurements or sampling were carried out by qualified staff. — printed p.13

fields.description: All measures from §4.4 documented; results carried over to the IGC-Cards for the value of the collected data (§5.2).
fields.verification_quote: All measures described under Item 4.4, which are carried out for quality control, must be documented concisely and extensively. This especially enables the operating staff and external staff to gain an objective impression of the quality of the collected data. The documentation can, for instance, be performed in the form of IQC-Cards, which record each quality control measure. — printed p.13

fields.description: Representative measuring results documented in a traceable, suitable form (§5.1).
fields.verification_quote: The measuring result must make a representative statement for the case of application. When quoting measuring results, if possible, only few digits should be used. Generally, two significant digits are quoted, e. g. 0.24; 2.4; 24, 240; 2400. — printed p.13

fields.label_de: Nachweis: Annex A, IQC-Card 2 - Internal Specifications
fields.verification_quote: Internal specifications allow the user to define individual quality targets (Section 4.4). The DWA Working Group IG-4.3 recommends minimum frequency, tolerances and quality targets (Sheet 1 of IQC-Card 2). The individual target should be documented in Sheets 2 and 3 of IQC-Card 2. The internal specifications should match the recommendations and could certainly be tightened. — printed p.22

fields.label_de: Nachweis: Annex A, IQC-Card 2 - Internal Specifications, Sheet 1 (minimum frequency)
fields.verification_quote: IQC-Card 2 Sheet 1 - Recommendations by the DWA-Working Group IG-4.3, col.3 Minimum frequency: Multiple determinations 1x per month, person- and matrix-related | Measurement of standards after each 10th sample; at least 1x per month, person-related | Plausibility checks (spiking, dilution) if measuring results are implausible; if matrix changes; 1x per quarter | Equivalency measurements and/or interlaboratory test (operating methods) 1x per year, person-related | Parallel measurements to the reference method 1x per year, method-related | Pipettes 100-1000 µl volume check 4x per year | pH-meter check 1x per month | Heating device/thermoblock check 1x per year — printed p.23

fields.label_de: Nachweis: Annex A, IQC-Card 2 - Internal Specifications, Sheet 1 (quality targets)
fields.verification_quote: IQC-Card 2 Sheet 1 - Recommendations by the DWA-Working Group IG-4.3, col.4 Quality target: Multiple determinations Random error < 10 % * | Measurement of standards Adherance to the permissible value range (control limits) | Plausibility checks (spiking, dilution) deviation < 20 % * | Equivalency measurements Deviation < 20 % * | Parallel measurements to the reference method Deviation < 20 % * | Pipettes 100-1000 µl Deviation < 2 % | Pipettes > 1000 µl Deviation < 1 % | pH-meter Deviation < 0.2 pH | Heating device/thermoblock Deviation < 3 °C | * For measuring results in the lower concentration range (e. g. Ptotal < 1 mg/l) greater percental tolerances are possible. In this case their permissible deviations should be defined in mg/l. — printed p.23

fields.label_de: Nachweis: Annex A, IQC-Card 9 - Testing Equipment Monitoring (Monitoring of the photometer)
fields.verification_quote: Monitoring of the photometer: Within the scope of testing equipment monitoring, the function of photometers must be tested regularly. The device must be checked annually according to the instructions manual. The test kit can be ordered as a test solution kit from the manufacturer of the photometer. The entire optical system of the photometers is checked. The monitoring must be documented on Sheet 1. — printed p.55

fields.description: Quality-assurance measure per IGC-Card 2 Sheet 1 (multiple determinations, measurement of standards, plausibility checks, equivalency, parallel, pipettes, pH-meter, heating device, measuring device).
fields.verification_quote: IQC-Card 2 Sheet 1 - Recommendations by the DWA-Working Group IG-4.3, col.1 Quality assurance measure: Multiple determinations | Measurement of standards | Plausibility checks (spiking, dilution) | Equivalency measurements and/or interlaboratory test (operating methods) | Parallel measurements to the reference method | Pipettes 100-1000 µl volume check | Pipettes > 1000 µl volume check | pH-meter check | Heating device/thermoblock check | Measuring device check (e.g. photometer) — printed p.23

fields.description: Minimum frequency for each QA measure per IGC-Card 2 Sheet 1 (e.g. multiple determinations 1x/month; measurement of standards after each 10th sample, at least 1x/month).

fields.description: Number of IGC-measures actually taken per parameter, recorded on the Survey Card (IGC-Card 1).
fields.verification_quote: To be able to recognise all performed quality assurance measures for a wastewater system quickly and reliably, a survey card must be produced. In a structured way it documents the overall measures that were taken within a certain period of time - similar to an annual report. [...] The information on the number of measures taken is therefore only entered at the end of this period. [...] To receive a relation of the IQC-measures taken for the samples analysed, also their number must be given. — printed p.18

fields.description: Calculated value = dilution factor * measured value diluted sample; compared to measured value original sample for plausibility (IGC-Card 5 Sheet 1, column 6).
fields.verification_quote: IQC-Card 5, Sheet 1 - Dilution: 2. Single steps: a) Determination of the MEASURED VALUE ORIGINAL SAMPLE (column 3) b) Dilution c) Determination of MEASURED VALUE DILUTED SAMPLE (column 5) | 3. Formulas for calculation: DILUTION FACTOR (column 4) = TOTAL VOLUME / SAMPLE VOLUME. CALCULATED VALUE (column 6) = DILUTION FACTOR · MEASURED VALUE DILUTED SAMPLE | If the variation between CALCULATED VALUE and MEASURED VALUE ORIGINAL SAMPLE is smaller than given in the internal specification (IQC-Card 2), there is no error in the matrix. If it is greater, an error in the matrix is likely. — printed p.35

fields.description: Concentration of the added standard solution (IGC-Card 5 Sheet 3 NSS formula).
fields.verification_quote: IQC-Card 5, Sheet 3 - standard addition (general procedure): 2. Single steps: Determination of the MEASURED VALUE ORIGINAL SAMPLE (column 3), Standard addition by adding the VOLUME STANDARD (column 5) in familiar CONCENTRATION STANDARD (column 6) to the defined VOLUME SAMPLE (column 4), Determination of MEASURED VALUE SPIKED SAMPLE (column 9). | 3. Calculation: NOMINAL VALUE SPIKED SAMPLE (NSS, column 8): NSS = [(volume sample · measured value original sample) + (volume standard · concentration standard)] / (volume sample + volume standard) — printed p.36

fields.description: Reference control measure (e.g. external standard) against which the single-determination difference is compared (IGC-Card 3 column 10).
fields.verification_quote: The greatest difference in the single measured values is entered into the IQC-Card in mg/l (column 8) and in % (greatest difference of the single measured values divided by the mean value; column 9). In column 10 the result of the control measure is documented. — printed p.29

fields.label_en: Deviation of single value from mean, %
fields.description: Deviation of a single value from the mean, compared to the quality target (IGC-Card 3).
fields.verification_quote: The greatest difference in the single measured values is entered into the IQC-Card in mg/l (column 8) and in % (greatest difference of the single measured values divided by the mean value; column 9). In column 10 the result of the control measure is documented. | IQC-Card 3 - Multiple Determinations (form header): 1 Date | 2 Name | 3 Sample designation | 4 Measured value 1 [mg/l] | 5 Measured value 2 [mg/l] | 6 Measured value 3 [mg/l] | 7 Mean [mg/l] | 8 Greatest spread Difference [mg/l] | 9 Greatest spread Col 8 x 100% / Col 7 [%] | 10 Interpretation: Quality target achieved? — printed p.29 and 30

fields.description: Mean of the single determination results; control measure value (IGC-Card 3).
fields.verification_quote: From the single results a mean value must be produced, which represents the measuring result. Here, all single results must be included in the mean. | From the single measured values the mean (add single measured values and divide them by the number of the measured values; column 7) is produced. | IQC-Card 3 - Multiple Determinations (form header): 1 Date | 2 Name | 3 Sample designation | 4 Measured value 1 [mg/l] | 5 Measured value 2 [mg/l] | 6 Measured value 3 [mg/l] | 7 Mean [mg/l] | 8 Greatest spread Difference [mg/l] | 9 Greatest spread Col 8 x 100% / Col 7 [%] | 10 Interpretation: Quality target achieved? — printed p.29 and 30

fields.description: Measured value of the diluted sample (column 5), multiplied by the dilution factor to get the calculated value (IGC-Card 5 Sheet 1).
fields.verification_quote: IQC-Card 5, Sheet 1 - Dilution: 2. Single steps: a) Determination of the MEASURED VALUE ORIGINAL SAMPLE (column 3) b) Dilution c) Determination of MEASURED VALUE DILUTED SAMPLE (column 5) | 3. Formulas for calculation: DILUTION FACTOR (column 4) = TOTAL VOLUME / SAMPLE VOLUME. CALCULATED VALUE (column 6) = DILUTION FACTOR · MEASURED VALUE DILUTED SAMPLE — printed p.35

fields.description: Measured value of the original (un-spiked) sample; input to the NSS computation and dilution comparison (IGC-Card 5).
fields.verification_quote: IQC-Card 5, Sheet 1 - Dilution: 2. Single steps: a) Determination of the MEASURED VALUE ORIGINAL SAMPLE (column 3) b) Dilution c) Determination of MEASURED VALUE DILUTED SAMPLE (column 5) | 3. requirements.description: The operating method shall be used only for the practical application of operating analysis (self-monitoring) within the scope of the standard.
requirements.source_quote: Besides the action on the practical application of operating methods, this Standard defines quality requirements that - if implemented - allow equal treatment. By taking into account these measures, the operating methods correspond to the requirements of § 4 AbwV (German Waste Water Ordinance); there are no reasons that oppose their application as equal methods in the determination in the discharge consent from a metrological point of view.

requirements.description: Analytical quality assurance (AQA: internal + external) shall be applied to the operating analysis.
requirements.source_quote: Analytical Quality Assurance (AQA): Measures for supporting own research results under controlled conditions. Analytical quality assurance comprises internal and external quality control.

requirements.description: The operating method shall be evaluated for the whole working range and, where possible, validated.
requirements.source_quote: The analyses within the scope of the operating monitoring of wastewater systems need to be evaluated whether the efforts made are justifiable or not. The application of operating methods decisively contributes to solving the problem. ... To notice such disturbing influences, the corresponding measures must be taken regularly, which are described in this Standard and which assure quality (plausibility checks, parallel analyses).

requirements.description: The manufacturer shall provide comprehensible work and user instructions for the method.
requirements.source_quote: Information on the expiry date and the storage conditions of the reagents must be attached to the packing in a clearly visible way.

requirements.description: The manufacturer shall provide an appropriate function control for the operating analysis system.
requirements.source_quote: Advice on an appropriate function control (inspection equipment monitoring) must be given.

requirements.description: Changes in handling (e.g. factor alterations) shall be communicated up-to-date and clearly.
requirements.source_quote: Changes in the handling (e. g. factor alterations in the photometric determination) must be communicated up-to-date and clearly.

requirements.title_de: User applies method per instruction leaflet
requirements.title_en: User applies method per instruction leaflet
requirements.description: The user shall apply the method exactly as described in the operating instruction leaflet.
requirements.source_quote: The user must be aware of the fact that also when applying the operating methods properly incorrect measurements higher results or lower results) can occur due to the composition of the sample. Due to quality assurance measures the user should be able to notice such incorrect measurements and to prevent them.

requirements.description: The user shall regularly perform the internal quality-control measures (IGC) per Annex A.
requirements.source_quote: When applying operating methods, the operator must take or organise the following measures together with the operating personnel: a) basic instruction, b) successive supervision, c) regular training measures, d) provision of written operating instructions for all important working steps, e) regular quality control.

requirements.description: The selected operating method shall be suitable per the criteria of Sections 3.1/3.2 and §4.2.
requirements.source_quote: By referring to the criteria mentioned in Sections 3.1 and 3.2, the operator must decide for the operating method that is suitable for his specific case of application. In doing so, especially the measuring range must be selected in such way that pre-eminently the expected result can be found in the 20 % to 80 % interval of the measuring range. From experience, this range shows the greatest analytical reliability. Suitable dilution steps are permitted.

requirements.title_de: Expected result within 20-80 % interval of measuring range
requirements.title_en: Expected result within 20-80 % interval of measuring range
requirements.description: Source S4.2: the measuring range must be selected in such way that preferably the expected result can be found in the 20 % to 80 % interval of the measuring range (suitable dilution steps permitted). This is NOT an "at least 80 % coverage" rule; it concerns placement of the expected result within a two-sided 20-80 % band. Field validation_range_coverage_pct does not match this concept.
requirements.source_quote: In doing so, especially the measuring range must be selected in such way that pre-eminently the expected result can be found in the 20 % to 80 % interval of the measuring range. From experience, this range shows the greatest analytical reliability. Suitable dilution steps are permitted.

requirements.description: Intensive basic instruction of staff shall be carried out (overview, preservation/sampling, practical exercise, sources of error).
requirements.source_quote: An intensive basic instruction must be carried out according to the following factors: overview of the parameters to be analysed; introduction to parameter-specific sampling including the required pre-treatment of samples and preservation; practice of the operating method for each parameter with representative wastewater samples of the planned cases of application (autonomous completion and handling) according to the given work instruction.

requirements.description: Instruction shall be updated/repeated at regular intervals (successive supervision).
requirements.source_quote: The skills and knowledge imparted in the basic instruction must be deepened and updated in regular training. Special importance must be attached to the thorough gathering, documentation, and interpretation of the measuring results. ... For seizing the results of operating methods, regular training courses (e. g. annually) are necessary.

requirements.description: Staff should attend training on proper use of pipettes/measuring ranges, equipment checks and IGC-Cards.
Quality controls / plausibility of results shall be carried out: sample suitability, multiple determination, parallel/equivalency comparison, blank+standard control, reagent storage life.
requirements.source_quote: When using operating methods, the operator must pay special attention to quality control (see also Annex A). This ensures that the handling, the reagents used and the measuring equipment are checked regularly as follows: check of the reproducibility of a sample by multiple determination; measuring of standard solutions to check the procedure, the measurement equipment and reagents; ... check of plausibility by dilution and standard addition of the wastewater sample; ... control of the reagents' storage life.

requirements.description: A representative sample of the correct type shall be taken and preserved/pre-treated and stored per IGC-Card 8 to slow changes before analysis.
requirements.source_quote: In most cases, the user of operating methods will carry out the sampling/pre-treatment of samples him-/herself.

requirements.description: Sampling and on-site assessment should follow the cited sampling standards (DIN 38402 Part 11; DIN EN ISO 5667-1/-2/-3); detailed sampling methods are owned by those standards.
Representative measuring results shall be documented in a traceable, suitable form.
requirements.source_quote: Taking into account the above listed notes on quality control is a prerequisite for correct analysis results of a constant high quality. However, the data only achieves an adequate meaning if the circumstances of their survey and the further measures taken for quality assurance are documented in a suitable form, e. g. by means of IQC-Cards.

requirements.description: All quality-control measures (per §4.4) shall be documented and carried over to the IGC-Cards.
requirements.source_quote: All measures described under Item 4.4, which are carried out for quality control, must be documented concisely and extensively. This especially enables the operating staff and external staff to gain an objective impression of the quality of the collected data. The documentation can, for instance, be performed in the form of IQC-Cards, which record each quality control measure.

requirements.description: An up-to-date overview of staff qualification and training measures shall be maintained.
requirements.source_quote: Within the scope of the documentation, a constant up-to-date overview of the staff's qualification as well as of the participation in regular training measures should be kept. This allows the proof that measurements or sampling were carried out by qualified staff.

requirements.description: Detected deviations, their cause, the corrective measure and result shall be recorded (IGC-Card 11) to support optimisation of the operating analysis.

Calculated value (dilution factor * measured value diluted sample) shall agree with the measured value of the original sample within the quality target; else check pipettes/process/measurement and repeat.
requirements.source_quote: Internal specifications allow the user to define individual quality targets (Section 4.4). The DWA Working Group IG-4.3 recommends minimum frequency, tolerances and quality targets (Sheet 1 of IQC-Card 2). The individual target should be documented in Sheets 2 and 3 of IQC-Card 2. The internal specifications should match the recommendations and could certainly be tightened.

requirements.clause_reference: Annex A, IQC-Card 2 - Internal Specifications, Sheet 1 (minimum frequency)
requirements.description: The measured value of the spiked sample shall lie within the confidence interval of the nominal value spiked sample (NSS); outside indicates a matrix error.
requirements.source_quote: Multiple determinations - 1x per month, person- and matrix-related; Measurement of standards - after each 10th sample, at least 1x per month, person-related; Plausibility checks (spiking, dilution) - if measuring results are implausible / if matrix changes, 1x per quarter; Equivalency measurements - 1x per year, person-related; Parallel measurements to the reference method - 1x per year, method-related.

requirements.clause_reference: Annex A, IQC-Card 2 - Internal Specifications, Sheet 1 (quality targets)
requirements.description: Each item of testing equipment shall be monitored at least at the frequency given in IGC-Card 9 (manufacturer/legislator frequency takes precedence if defined).
requirements.source_quote: Multiple determinations - Random error < 10 %; Plausibility checks - Deviation < 20 %; Equivalency measurements - Deviation < 20 %; Parallel measurements to the reference method - Deviation < 20 %. For measuring results in the lower concentration range (e. g. P-tot < 1 mg/l) greater percental tolerances are possible. In this case their permissible deviations should be defined in mg/l.

requirements.clause_reference: Annex A, IQC-Card 9 - Testing Equipment Monitoring (Monitoring of the photometer)
requirements.description: The photometer function shall be checked annually with the manufacturer's test-solution kit; deviation beyond permitted -> mark defective and call manufacturer.
requirements.source_quote: Monitoring of the photometer: Within the scope of testing equipment monitoring, the function of photometers must be tested regularly. The device must be checked annually according to the instructions manual. The test kit can be ordered as a test solution kit from the manufacturer of the photometer. The entire optical system of the photometers is checked. The monitoring must be documented on Sheet 1.

requirements.description: Reference analytical methods (DIN 38404/38405/38406/38409, DIN EN 1899 etc.) cited in the Literature section define the reference values used for equivalency/parallel comparison.
For a multiple determination, the deviation of a single value from the mean shall be within the quality target (% deviation).
requirements.source_quote: The greatest difference is decisive for the interpretation of the multiple determination. If the difference lies within the quality target, the spread is ok. If the difference is greater, the entire multiple determination should be repeated. [VC]

requirements.description: The deviation of the operating-method measured value from the reference-method nominal value (%) shall be within the quality target.
requirements.source_quote: Usually, the deviation in the central measurement range should not exceed the quality target of ≤ 20 % (in this regard also see IQC-Card 2: Internal Specifications). [VC]

requirements.description: The deviation between operating-method and reference-method values (%) shall be within the quality target.
requirements.source_quote: Usually, the deviation in the central measuring range should not exceed the quality target of ≤ 20 % (see also IQC-Card 2 in this regard: Internal Specifications). [VC]

requirements.description: A piston-stroke pipette shall be within its permissible deviation (<=2 % for 0.100-0.500 ml; <=1 % for 1.000-5.000 ml); outside -> remove from testing equipment and send to manufacturer.
requirements.source_quote: The mean value must lie within a defined tolerance range (see table). Tested volume [ml] / Deviation [%] / Tolerance range [g]: 0.100 / ≤ 2 / 0.098 – 0.102; 0.200 / ≤ 2 / 0.196 – 0.204; 0.500 / ≤ 2 / 0.490 – 0.510; 1.000 / ≤ 1 / 0.990 – 1.010; 2.000 / ≤ 1 / 1.980 – 2.020; 5.000 / ≤ 1 / 4.950 – 5.050. If the results lie outside the tolerance range, the pipette must no longer be used as testing equipment (remove designation) and should be sent to the manufacturer for testing, if necessary. [VC]

requirements.description: The heating device/thermoblock temperature deviation shall be < 3 degC at 100 degC and 148 degC.
requirements.source_quote: Within the scope of testing equipment monitoring, the function of thermoblocks must be checked annually. Check of the required temperatures of 100 °C and/or 148 °C (± 3 °C). Alternatively, also other/further frequently used temperatures can be tested. [VC]
